subject: Controlled kernel switchover & staggered node restarts — planned window and mitigation
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Acme Data - Alan Cho <alan.cho@acmedata.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Controlled kernel switchover & staggered node restarts — planned window and mitigation

Hi Alan,

We wanted to give you an early heads-up about a planned, controlled kernel switchover and driver refresh across our us-west serving pools. This is part of a safety update that resolves a kernel-level I/O regression we've been tracking.

Planned window (staggered):
- Mar 31, 2027 — 02:00 to 06:00 UTC (us-west pools only)
- We will perform rolling restarts in small batches (approx. 30 minutes per node-pool) to keep latency SLOs intact.

What to expect:
- Short pod restarts per instance (expected disruption: 2–5 minutes for a single request path while kernel swap completes).
- KV/prefix cache: we will warm caches proactively and maintain in-flight sessions where possible; long lived pinned sessions may be reattached.
- Dedicated/reserved pools: we will not touch Dedicated pools that are explicitly pinned and under contractual isolation unless you opt-in; please see the attached CSV for instances we plan to touch by default.

Mitigation & rollback:
- We have a validated rollback image and a pre-tested rollback plan in the attached runbook.
- Automatic fallback policy: if error rates for any pool exceed thresholds, traffic will be routed to the next-compatible model variant in another region or to a pinned standby pool.

Action items for Acme Data:
1) Review the attached affected-instances-us-west.csv and flag any instance IDs to exclude by EOD Mar 29.
2) Let us know if you have scheduled batch jobs between 02:00–06:00 UTC on Mar 31 so we can coordinate.

Attachments: runbook-kernel-switchover-20270328.pdf (operational steps), affected-instances-us-west.csv
Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2027-03-28-kernel-switchover

If you'd like us to entirely avoid touching your Dedicated pools, reply with the pool IDs and we will mark them as excluded. We aim to minimize impact and will send a completion note + brief postmortem within 24 hours after the window.

Thanks — Ben

--
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Customer Reliability

Date: 2027-03-28T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Controlled kernel switchover & staggered node restarts — planned window and mitigation

Ben — thanks for the heads-up. A couple quick questions: 
1) Will existing KV cache entries persist across the node restart, or will clients need to repopulate prefixes? We run latency-sensitive lookups and want to avoid cache-warm spikes.
2) Our reserved Dedicated pool (pool-d-acme-01) has nightly jobs that kick off at 03:15 UTC — will that be touched if we don't explicitly exclude it?

If you can confirm rollback time and an SLA for detection -> rollback threshold (what error rate triggers fallback), that would help our SREs plan.

Also, please confirm whether the runbook includes steps for seamless reconnection for long-running chat sessions.

— Alan
Alan Cho
Head of Platform, Acme Data
alan.cho@acmedata.com

Subject: Re: Controlled kernel switchover & staggered node restarts — planned window and mitigation

Hi Alan — great questions, answered inline below.

1) KV cache persistence:
- Short answer: we expect most in-memory prefix/KV cache entries to be lost on a kernel-level restart. To compensate we are pre-warming caches from a snapshot and prioritizing hot prefixes for Acme Data during the first 20 minutes after each pool is brought back. We will also throttle background jobs to avoid a thundering herd.

2) Dedicated pool impact:
- By default we do NOT include explicitly reserved Dedicated pools in the rolling driver update unless the pool is listed in the affected CSV. I checked pool-d-acme-01 — it is NOT on our default touch list. If you prefer, we can add it to an opt-in maintenance rotation during a later, strictly scheduled window.

Rollback & thresholds:
- Detection window: 5-minute rolling error-rate and latency spike monitors.
- Trigger: if error-rate > 2.5% or 99th p99 latency increases by > 200ms sustained for 5 minutes, we will initiate automated rollback for the affected node-pool and route traffic to standby pools.
- Rollback time: typical rollback completes within 8–12 minutes once initiated (we've exercised this path during rehearsals).

Long-running sessions:
- The runbook contains a reconnection handshake we push to SDKs; most SDKs will transparently reconnect. We will also send a small client-side library patch (non-breaking) later this week that improves reconnect backoff and prioritizes session restoration for Acme Data.

Next steps: please confirm whether you want pool-d-acme-01 excluded (default: excluded) and flag any instance IDs to keep out of the window by Mar 29 EOD. We'll set up a brief runbook walkthrough (15 minutes) if you'd like.

Ben

--

Date: 2027-03-28T17:20:00-07:00
Subject: Maintenance window completed — short summary & postmortem follow-up

Alan / team — quick update: the scheduled kernel switchover and rolling restarts for the us-west pools completed successfully within the announced window.

Summary:
- Window: Mar 31, 02:00–05:45 UTC (we finished 15 minutes early by operating one fewer fallback step).
- Impact: transient 2–6 minute restart events for touched instances. No sustained error-rate breaches for Acme Data pools.
- Dedicated pools: pool-d-acme-01 was not touched per your default exclusion.

What we tracked and next steps:
- We observed a small, transient cache-warm spike immediately after two early pool restarts; automated throttling prevented customer-visible degradation.
- We are publishing a short postmortem (digest) and the full runbook plus measured telemetry to the Drive link below.
- Postmortem review: scheduled Mar 31, 2027 20:00 UTC — invite sent to your SREs and our on-call.

Links:
- Postmortem digest: https://drive.google.com/link-to/postmortem-20270331
- Runbook & telemetry: https://drive.google.com/link-to/runbook
- Status: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2027-03-28-kernel-switchover

If you saw anything anomalous on your side, please reply to this thread or raise the item in the postmortem. We will keep this thread for coordination and will export a short executive summary for renewals if helpful.

Thanks for coordinating with us — Ben
